bol_001: You can recognise them by their thick trunks, several over four metres round, lining the park's two concentric paths. They stand in Parco della Montagnola.
bol_002: You can recognise it by being visibly taller than everything around it, long before you reach the lake it stands beside. It stands in the Giardini Margherita.
bol_003: You can recognise it by its height, 39.5 metres, the tallest monumental tree in the whole province, rising directly behind the Minghetti statue. It stands in Piazza Minghetti.
bol_004: You can recognise it by growing in a garden raised more than four metres above the piazza below, close by the Rusconi family's palazzo. It stands in Piazza Malpighi.
bol_005: You can recognise it by its drooping branch tips and height near 30 metres, in the garden framing the hospital building. It stands at the Istituto Ortopedico Rizzoli.
bol_006: You can recognise it by its fan-shaped leaves turning a uniform, near-luminous yellow within days each autumn, unlike anything else on this list. It stands in Piazza Cavour.
bol_008: You can recognise it by standing taller than the low funerary monuments around it, directly over Carducci's plain granite tomb. It stands in the Certosa di Bologna.
bol_009: You can recognise it by dominating the open meadow in front of the villa, with visible lightning-strike scarring on part of its crown. It stands in the Parco di Villa Ghigi.
bol_012: You can recognise it as the largest tree in the garden, its foliage held in flat, ascending, tiered plates. It stands in the gardens of Villa delle Rose.
